title: Parameter-Free Deep Sub-Ångstrom Resolution Electron Ptychography Reconstructions using Neural Networks
content: Electron ptychography has gained significant recent attention because it can exceed the diffraction-limited resolution of aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), even in uncorrected STEMs [1,2]. Electron ptychography reconstructs an image from 4D-STEM dataset obtained by collecting a series of convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) patterns as an electron beam is scanned across a sample. The most common approaches to ptychography reconstructions utilize iterative phase retrieval techniques, which have achieved reconstructions with resolutions on the order of tens of picometers. However, successfully reconstructing a high-quality, converged object is often challenging, time consuming, and requires precise knowledge of acquisition parameters such as the convergence angle, defocus, and scan step size. Machine learning (ML) models have the potential to significantly speed up ptychography reconstructions and reduce the manual intervention involved in the reconstruction process. While other works have employed neural networks for object reconstruction from diffraction patterns [3-5], there have not been any models trained specifically on 4D STEM data. Training a model exclusively on 4D-STEM data should enable the neural network to focus on learning subtle information relevant to atomic resolution ptychography.
